title: Read validation shard payloads for variance analysis
author: sylvesterkaczmarek
body:
## Problem

The variance-analysis command reads a training shard as raw uint16 values, including its 1024-byte header. This adds 512 metadata-derived token IDs to the sample, displaces validation tokens, and hides out-of-vocabulary values by clipping them. The statistics therefore describe altered input.

## Change

Reuse the existing baseline shard reader, then take the same 8192-token prefix. Reject out-of-vocabulary IDs in that prefix instead of rewriting them. Preserve model loading, hooks, variance calculation, command-line arguments, and output structure. No training-script or archived-submission changes.

## Validation

- **14 tests passed**. Thirteen fail on unchanged source; the missing-file control passes before and after.
- Tests exercise main with real synthetic shard and checkpoint files. They cover header exclusion, prefix boundaries, malformed headers, inconsistent lengths, and invalid IDs.
- An integration case uses a tiny synthetic PyTorch module with real forward hooks, comparing the resulting statistics with an independent NumPy calculation.
- Syntax/error checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- Run `python -m pytest tests/test_variance_shard_input.py` with the baseline dependencies and pytest installed.

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.14.1, and NumPy 2.5.3 on macOS arm64 CPU. No pretrained weights, external datasets, full training, or GPU evaluation was used. This establishes input fidelity without claiming changes to published results. No dependency changes.

Reproduced against `f5c079314c4877fbb0af378c0abade5a8ca33d3a`.
